title: Micro Mentor Sprint: Hire Ramp & Early Success Playbook
body:
Purpose: Quick, pragmatic playbook for running a 14-day micro-mentor sprint that accelerates new hires from orientation to measurable contributor code/review/work outputs. Designed for IC hires across eng/product/design who need an evidence-backed 2-week ramp and a lightweight interview/eval artifact set for hiring calibrations and manager check-ins.

Scope: Applied to all cross-functional IC hires (L3-L5) where we want a fast, hands-on immersion run with an assigned mentor. Not intended for leadership onboarding, long internships, or contractors longer than 3 months.

Outcomes we care about (14d):
- Clear first deliverable defined and shipped (or PR opened + review comments)
- Mentor & hire subjective readiness score (1–5) with short evidence bullets
- Collection of 3 interview-evidence snippets that map to the hiring rubric (technical, collaboration, ownership)
- Manager decision checkpoint: continue 30/60/90 plan OR remediation plan

Roles & expectations:
- New hire: Follow the 14-day checklist, capture evidence in the "first-14-days" doc, ask for help early.
- Mentor (assigned for 14 days): daily 30-min pairing/check-in, owns day-by-day tasks, ensures access, leaves review comments, captures 3 evidence bullets for rubric.
- Manager: sets first deliverable, checks in day 7 and day 14 for calibration, clears blockers.
- People Ops: provides kickoff template, intro email, and feedback collection at day 14.

Kickoff (Day 0-1):
- People Ops sends: welcome email (access checklist, Slack intros, mentor + manager contact)
- Mentor runs a 60-min orientation: repo tour, infra basics, dev flow, where to find docs, how to run tests locally
- Confirm hardware/access (vpn, infra creds, ticketing)
- Quick goal-setting: define a scoped "first deliverable" that can be demoed or submitted as PR in 7–14 days (target: small feature, bugfix, infra cleanup, doc + script)

Day 2-7 (focused get-to-green):
- Daily 15–30m sync: unblock + pairing note
- Small tasks that exercise codepath + CI: write 1 unit test, add a tiny endpoint or fix a flaky test, add a helpful comment to shared README
- Mentor: leave inline review comments, escalate infra issues to SRE/infra as needed
- Evidence capture: at least 1 technical snippet (code PR link), 1 collaboration snippet (review thread or Slack excerpt)

Midpoint (Day 7) — Manager checkpoint:
- Manager + Mentor + Hire: 30-min review
- Questions: Is the deliverable feasible? Does the hire know the deploy/test flow? Any access/blockers? Is the ramp on track?
- Output: Update 1–2 prioritized actions for next week (e.g., pair on deploy, expand test coverage)

Day 8-14 (ship/demo & reflect):
- Finish or open the PR for first deliverable; include test and basic docs
- Mentor does focused pairing on any remaining unknowns (token management, observability hooks, console dashboards)
- Collect evidence packets: 3 short bullets mapping to rubric (technical, ownership, communication) with links

Day 14 — Readout & Calibration:
- 30–45m readout: hire demos PR/feature + mentor highlights and manager gives initial readiness rating (1–5)
- People Ops collects post-sprint feedback form (3 questions + free text)
- Decision: proceed with standard 30/60/90 OR agree remediation plan (2-week extension with concrete milestones)

Interview & Evidence Rubric (quick):
- Technical correctness (1–5): quality of code, tests, and design tradeoffs. Evidence: link to PR + 2 inline notes.
- Collaboration (1–5): how they solicit feedback, incorporate comments, communicate blockers. Evidence: Slack thread or review convo snippet.
- Ownership (1–5): picks up tasks, drives to completion, proactively asks for next steps. Evidence: timeline of task + final PR/issue.
- Learning velocity (1–5): uptake of feedback and context familiarity. Evidence: before/after checklist of infra skills.

Scoring guidance (mentor notes to self):
- 5: Clear independent contributor; few mentor prompts; produced high-quality PR and helped improve others' work.
- 3: Needs some scaffolding but shows consistent progress and good responses to feedback.
- 1–2: Significant blockers; needs structured remediation (extend sprint or pair program).

Templates to copy (quick links & local snippets):
- Kickoff email subject: "Welcome to Redwood — Your Micro-Mentor Sprint (Mentor: NAME)" (include 1-2 sentence deliverable and 1st pairing slot)
- Evidence capture format (in the hire's doc): 1) Link, 2) 1-sentence summary, 3) Which rubric dimension it maps to, 4) Why it matters
- Manager day7 template: 5 bullet status + 2 blockers + 1 ask

Common blockers & remediation playbook:
- Missing infra access: escalate to infra on RED-xxxx, mentor files a follow-up, propose a temporary stub task if access >48h
- Overly ambitious deliverable: re-scope to an MVP with clear acceptance criteria
- Social onboarding lag: invite the hire to 2 cross-functional syncs and assign a co-reviewer

Notes to self / unresolved questions: 
- Should we formally tie this to hiring scorecards? Pros: richer interview evidence. Cons: conflates onboarding safety with hiring judgment. Proposed: keep readout separate but attach anonymized evidence to hiring repo if both manager and hire agree.
- Consider a "pairing passport" micro-badge after 3 successful pairs — track as a lightweight recognition.

Appendix: Example day-by-day micro-checklist (copy into hire doc) — very low friction.
- Day 0: confirm accounts, intro channels, meet mentor
- Day 1: local dev run, run tests, review repo layout with mentor
- Day 2: small bug/task — open PR draft
- Day 3: pairing session on feature/deploy path
- Day 4–5: write tests + address initial review comments
- Day 6: CI passes locally, iterate on review feedback
- Day 7: manager checkpoint + update plan
- Day 8–12: polish, docs, add observability hooks
- Day 13: final PR ready, write 1-paragraph postmortem/learnings
- Day 14: readout, scorecards submitted, feedback form sent

Contact: Priya Kapoor (people-ops), Derek Chen (mentor program ops).

Quick links: Confluence: /display/HR/Mentor+Program+Overview, Jira: RED-1427 (micro-mentor sprint pilot), GitHub onboarding repo: github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding-scripts

End — keep this light; iterate after two pilot cohorts.

(Notes: informal — leave open questions in the Confluence page. This doc is intentionally terse for copy/paste into hire onboarding docs.)
